questions.title: Manual String Length
questions.description:
Measure a string by walking it, one character at a time (do NOT call len — that is the point of the drill).

Implement only this function:

    def string_length(s):

It must count the characters with a loop and return the count.

Input Format:
One line with the string.

Output Format:
One line with the length.

Constraints:
1 <= len(s) <= 1000

count = 0
for ch in s:

questions.title: Detective Phrase Anagram
questions.description:
A detective compares two PHRASES for anagram matches ignoring spaces and letter case ("Dormitory Dirty" vs "Dirty Room").

Implement only this function:

    def is_phrase_anagram(a, b):

It must return True when both phrases contain exactly the same letters after lowercasing and stripping spaces. Lowercasing via .lower() is expected.

Input Format:
Line 1: phrase A.
Line 2: phrase B.

Output Format:
One line with True or False.

Constraints:
1 <= len(a), len(b) <= 100, phrases contain letters and spaces

b = input()


def is_phrase_anagram(a, b):
    na = "".join(a.lower().split())
    nb = "".join(b.lower().split())
    return sorted(na) == sorted(nb)

def is_phrase_palindrome(s):
    cleaned = "".join(ch.lower() for ch in s if ch.isalnum())
    return cleaned == cleaned[::-1]

questions.title: Genetic Palindrome Scan
questions.description:
A genome lab scans a sequence for its longest palindromic substring; when several palindromes tie in length the LEFTMOST one is reported. Use the expand-around-center technique.

Implement only this function:

    def longest_palindrome(s):

It must return the longest palindromic substring (the leftmost on ties). Every single character is itself a palindrome, so the result is never empty.

Input Format:
One line with the sequence (lowercase letters).

Output Format:
One line with the longest palindromic substring.

Constraints:
1 <= len(s) <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
s = input()


def longest_palindrome(s):
    n = len(s)
    best_start = 0
    best_len = 1
    for center in range(n):
        left = center
        right = center
        while left >= 0 and right < n and s[left] == s[right]:
            left -= 1
            right += 1
        if right - left - 1 > best_len:
            best_len = right - left - 1
            best_start = left + 1
        left = center
        right = center + 1
        while left >= 0 and right < n and s[left] == s[right]:
            left -= 1
            right += 1
        if right - left - 1 > best_len:
            best_len = right - left - 1
            best_start = left + 1
    return s[best_start:best_start + best_len]


print(longest_palindrome(s))
